passage.text: In both Thailand and Canada, school is compulsory for children.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈboʊθ ˈtaɪlænd ənd ˈkænədə, ˈskuːl ɪz kəmˈpʌlsəri fər ˈtʃɪldrən.

passage.text: Most students go to school for about twelve years and finish high school at seventeen or eighteen.
passage.reading: ˈmoʊst ˈstuːdənts ˈɡoʊ tə ˈskuːl fər əˈbaʊt ˈtwɛlv ˈjɪrz ənd ˈfɪnɪʃ ˈhaɪ ˌskuːl ət ˌsɛvənˈtiːn ɔːr ˌeɪˈtiːn.

passage.text: But school life in the two countries is quite different.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈskuːl ˈlaɪf ɪn ðə ˈtuː ˈkʌntriz ɪz ˈkwaɪt ˈdɪfərənt.

passage.text: In Thailand, students wear a uniform, and every morning they stand in lines outside before class.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈtaɪlænd, ˈstuːdənts ˈwɛr ə ˈjuːnəfɔːrm, ənd ˈɛvri ˈmɔːrnɪŋ ðeɪ ˈstænd ɪn ˈlaɪnz ˌaʊtˈsaɪd bɪˈfɔːr ˈklæs.

passage.text: In Canada, most students do not wear a uniform, and they can wear jeans and T-shirts to school.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈkænədə, ˈmoʊst ˈstuːdənts duː ˈnɑːt ˈwɛr ə ˈjuːnəfɔːrm, ənd ðeɪ kən ˈwɛr ˈdʒiːnz ənd ˈtiːʃɜːrts tə ˈskuːl.

passage.text: Thai classes are often big, with forty or fifty students in one room.
passage.reading: ˈtaɪ ˈklæsɪz ər ˈɔːfən ˈbɪɡ, wɪð ˈfɔːrti ɔːr ˈfɪfti ˈstuːdənts ɪn ˈwʌn ˈruːm.

passage.text: A Canadian class usually has about twenty-five students, and they often discuss ideas in groups.
passage.reading: ə kəˈneɪdiən ˈklæs ˈjuːʒuəli ˈhæz əˈbaʊt ˈtwɛnti ˈfaɪv ˈstuːdənts, ənd ðeɪ ˈɔːfən dɪˈskʌs aɪˈdiːəz ɪn ˈɡruːps.

passage.text: The biggest difference is the university entrance exam.
passage.reading: ðə ˈbɪɡɪst ˈdɪfrəns ɪz ðə ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəti ˈɛntrəns ɪɡˌzæm.

passage.text: In Thailand, students have to pass a difficult entrance exam to get into a good university.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈtaɪlænd, ˈstuːdənts ˈhæf tə ˈpæs ə ˈdɪfɪkəlt ˈɛntrəns ɪɡˌzæm tə ˈɡɛt ˈɪntuː ə ˈɡʊd ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəti.

passage.text: Many students study with a tutor in the evenings and on weekends, even though they are already tired after school.
passage.reading: ˈmɛni ˈstuːdənts ˈstʌdi wɪð ə ˈtuːtər ɪn ði ˈiːvnɪŋz ənd ɑːn ˈwiːkɛndz, ˌiːvən ˈðoʊ ðeɪ ər ɔːlˈrɛdi ˈtaɪərd ˈæftər ˈskuːl.

passage.text: In Canada, there is no big entrance exam.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈkænədə, ðɛr ɪz ˈnoʊ ˈbɪɡ ˈɛntrəns ɪɡˌzæm.

passage.text: Universities look at students' grades from high school.
passage.reading: ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsətiz ˈlʊk ət ˈstuːdənts ˈɡreɪdz frəm ˈhaɪ ˌskuːl.

passage.text: So Canadian students have more free time, although they still have to work hard.
passage.reading: soʊ kəˈneɪdiən ˈstuːdənts ˈhæv ˈmɔːr ˈfriː ˈtaɪm, ɔːlˈðoʊ ðeɪ ˈstɪl ˈhæf tə ˈwɜːrk ˈhɑːrd.
